title: Middleware rewrite doesn't work with i18n

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue was opened via the bug report template.

body:
### What version of Next.js are you using?

12.0.2

### What version of Node.js are you using?

14.17.6

### What browser are you using?

Chrome

### What operating system are you using?

macOS

### How are you deploying your application?

next start

### Describe the Bug

Next 12 Middleware rewrite doesn't handle locale correctly with [i18n routing](https://nextjs.org/docs/advanced-features/i18n-routing) enabled. For example, if we rewrite `/test` to `/fr/test` using middleware, it will still show `/test` with the default locale because the locale info is lost during rewrite.

So you can't do this:
```ts
// in middleware
req.nextUrl.locale = detectedLocale;
return NextResponse.rewrite(req.nextUrl);
```

or equivalently this:
```ts
// in middleware
req.nextUrl.pathname = `/${detectedLocale}${req.nextUrl.pathname}`
return NextResponse.rewrite(req.nextUrl);
```

### Expected Behavior

The locale info should be parsed when rewriting from middleware. 

### To Reproduce

I modified the [vercel i18n example](https://github.com/vercel/examples/tree/main/edge-functions/i18n) to demonstrate the issue.

See: https://github.com/leethree/next-i18n-rewrite

Supposedly you have `fr` as your browser locale. When visiting the home page (http://localhost:3000/), it should show your current locale as detected: 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/648142/140086374-db47cab0-d8bd-484c-b777-3532ebe3fff5.png)

(ignore the flag, note the "locale: fr" below that.)

But actual behaviour:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/648142/140086682-b4376dda-af73-41d9-b560-4fc78ed8da71.png)
